expansion_contract.fact_row: verified official consumer-right, enforcement, affordability, complaint, contract or programme fact
expansion_contract.boundary_row: prevents account-level rights, enforcement findings, survey metrics, regional awards, build plans or rounded management information from being promoted to exact current postcode or parcel coverage without accepted r2 archive bytes and hardened postjoin evidence

facts.detail: Ofcom published the current money-saving guide on 1 July 2026.
Phone, broadband and pay-TV minimum terms are commonly 12, 18 or 24 months.
Providers must tell customers when a contract is ending and how much could be saved on a new deal.
Some gaining providers may offer money toward an existing early-termination charge.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract timing and switching incentives are customer-account evidence, not parcel coverage or measured speed.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Virgin Media enforcement decision published 8 July 2026

facts.detail: Ofcom fined Virgin Media £28 million for unreasonable barriers when customers tried to cancel or switch.
The investigation concluded that millions of cancellation calls were likely mishandled over nearly three years.
Findings included deliberate call dropping, excessive transfers and repeated unnecessary holds.
The commission scheme effectively encouraged and financially rewarded the problematic conduct.

guard_streams.write_limit: An enforcement outcome concerns switching conduct and cannot change parcel serviceability, technology or performance fields.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide updated 20 July 2026

facts.detail: The guide lists BT, EE, Hyperoptic, Plusnet, Sky including NOW, TalkTalk, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media, Vodafone and Zen.
Qualifying events cover delayed repair after total loss, missed appointments and delayed new-service starts.
After 30 days of payments a signatory may serve notice that automatic payments will stop after a further 30 days.
After a cease notice the provider must take reasonable steps to offer an alternative service; compensation continues if no suitable alternative is provided.

guard_streams.write_limit: Compensation eligibility and provider membership do not identify the network cause, exact fault location or parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom complaints resolution update published 8 April 2026

facts.detail: Strengthened rules allowing earlier ADR escalation took effect on 8 April 2026.
The unresolved-complaint waiting period was reduced from eight weeks to six weeks.
ADR schemes independently and impartially assess evidence from customers and providers.
Access to an Ofcom-approved ADR scheme is free for customers.

guard_streams.write_limit: Complaint escalation rules and adjudication access are consumer remedies, not parcel-level coverage evidence.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Communications Affordability Tracker updated 14 May 2026

facts.detail: The tracker monitors affordability experiences across home broadband, mobile, landline and pay-TV services.
Ofcom uses the tracker for regular monitoring of consumer affordability experiences and behaviours.
Financial vulnerability combines household income, working status and household size.
The publication suppresses certain demographic breakdowns where base sizes are too low.

guard_streams.write_limit: Survey-based affordability and vulnerability metrics cannot populate parcel price, speed, coverage or eligibility fields.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom business contracts guide updated 26 June 2026

facts.detail: A business contract may specify one fixed monthly price for the full term.
A contract may instead specify a dated increase with both prices stated in pounds and pence.
The monthly amounts payable during the contract should be given clearly before sign-up.
A price increase beyond the agreed contract requires at least one month notice and a penalty-free exit right.

guard_streams.write_limit: Business contract pricing and exit rights are not evidence of current parcel availability or measured network performance.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom broadband complaints update published 23 July 2026

facts.detail: The latest complaint figures cover January to March 2026.
Major-provider broadband complaints fell to six per 100,000 customers.
TalkTalk was the most complained-about fixed-broadband provider while Plusnet and Sky recorded the fewest complaints.
The figures compare major providers and are not premise, postcode or parcel performance measurements.

guard_streams.write_limit: Provider complaint rates and rankings must not alter parcel-level confidence, coverage or measured-speed fields.

facts.detail: The South Wiltshire Project Gigabit contract was awarded to Wessex Internet.
The award is £18.8 million for around 14,500 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in March 2024.
Trenching, duct and fibre work precede service requests and the premise scope can change after detailed planning or technical review.

guard_streams.write_limit: Award scope and anticipated construction do not establish current orderability at an individual parcel.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Cornwall contracts update dated 12 February 2026

facts.detail: Wildanet will no longer fully deliver the southwest and central Cornwall contracts.
The update reports around 13,200 premises covered to date under the two contracts.
Wildanet will not deliver the remaining 7,700 contracted premises.
BDUK is developing alternative plans with other suppliers for premises that were due to be covered.

guard_streams.write_limit: Partial delivery and supplier withdrawal leave individual remaining premises unresolved until replacement delivery evidence exists.

facts.detail: The Cumbria regional Project Gigabit contract was awarded to Fibrus.
The contract value is £108.5 million for up to 59,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed on 1 December 2022.
Residents and businesses can request service only after the gigabit-capable network has been built; detailed planning can change scope.

guard_streams.write_limit: A regional award and planned premise count do not prove current parcel coverage or connection status.

facts.detail: The North Northumberland contract was awarded to Borderlink.
The contract targets more than 3,750 premises.
The page distinguishes the North Northumberland award from the Teesdale contract and the wider North East procurement.
Premises can be outside planned scope because coverage exists, commercial or voucher plans apply, or delivery is too difficult or costly.

guard_streams.write_limit: Programme inclusion and exclusion reasons are planning evidence, not accepted current parcel serviceability.

facts.detail: The Teesdale contract was awarded to Borderlink, the parent company of GoFibre.
The award is £6.6 million for more than 4,000 premises.
The contract was signed on 22 September 2022.
Preparatory construction is required before service access and the premise scope remains subject to detailed planning and technical change.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract award, target count and construction sequence do not prove present parcel coverage.

facts.detail: The New Forest Project Gigabit contract was awarded to Wessex Internet.
The award is nearly £14 million for around 10,500 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in March 2023.
The page describes planned network build and lists existing coverage, commercial plans, voucher plans and cost difficulty as possible scope exclusions.

guard_streams.write_limit: Planned contract coverage cannot be promoted to a current parcel connection or speed record.

facts.detail: The framework page records a £159.2 million value for call-off one.
Call-off one initially listed 51,820 premises across Lancashire, West Berkshire, Staffordshire, Surrey, Hertfordshire, Wiltshire and Gloucestershire.
The call-off one contract date is 28 June 2024.
The page records January 2025 additions covering Shropshire, North Herefordshire, Wales, Devon, Somerset, Essex, North East England and Worcestershire areas.

guard_streams.write_limit: Framework values, geographic groupings and call-off dates are programme evidence, not exact current parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK May June and July 2026 contract tables

facts.detail: The monthly publications are snapshots of data held on 21 May, 17 June and 16 July 2026.
Contracted-premise figures include initial scope only and can omit deferred-scope premises.
The management tables are not directly comparable with BDUK official statistics because the measures serve different purposes.
Figures are rounded to the nearest ten and subject to variable ingestion lag, so they should not assess contractual milestones.

guard_streams.write_limit: Monthly management snapshots cannot identify address readiness, orderability or subsidy-caused parcel coverage.
